questions.question: The calendar for the year 1833 was the same for the year:
questions.solution:
The logic follows here is :

__
 
• A leap year repetition will be a on a leap year.
 
• A non-leap year repetition will be a on a non-leap year.
 
• A calendar year is repeated after every 7 odd days.
 
• No. of odd days in non-leap year = Remainder of (365 ÷ 7) = 1 odd days.
 
• No. of odd days in leap year = Remainder of (366 ÷ 7) = 2 odd days.

​Calculate the year gap with a multiple of 7.

If the leap year repetition comes after 7 odd days is also a leap year then it will be the answer, otherwise count for next multiple of 7. Same for the non-leap year also.

Explanation:

Here, the given year is 1833. It is a non-leap year, so we will count odd days from it:

1833 → 1 odd day

1834→ 1 odd day

1835 → 1 odd day

1836 → 2 odd days

1837 → 1 odd day

1838 → 1 odd day

Total = 7 odd days 

Thus, 1833 will be repeated after 7 odd days i.e. in 1839.

Hence, the correct answer is "1839".

questions.question: Which commission recommended creating a Permanent Secretariat for the Inter-State Council?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sarkaria Commission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Sarkaria Commission** was set up in **1983** by the Government of India to review the **Centre-State relations** and recommend changes to improve coordination between the Union and the States.
 
• The Commission recommended the creation of a **Permanent Secretariat for the Inter-State Council**. This was aimed at ensuring the council's smooth functioning and the continuity of its operations.
 
• The Inter-State Council is a constitutional body established under **Article 263** of the Indian Constitution. Its primary purpose is to promote coordination and cooperation between the Union and State governments.
 
• The Sarkaria Commission's recommendation for a Permanent Secretariat was to provide the council with **institutional support** and enhance its efficiency in addressing inter-governmental issues.
 
• The recommendation emphasized the need for a structured and well-organized mechanism to resolve disputes and improve Centre-State relations effectively.
 
• Although the Permanent Secretariat was not implemented immediately, the Sarkaria Commission's suggestions remain significant in the context of Centre-State relations in India.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Sarkaria Commission.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sarkaria Commission:**

 
 
• The **Sarkaria Commission** was established in **1983** and submitted its report in **1988**. Its primary objective was to review and analyze the working of the existing arrangements between the Union and the States.
 
• The Commission made several recommendations, including the creation of a **Permanent Secretariat** for the Inter-State Council to provide administrative and logistical support.
 
• The focus was on improving the efficiency of the council and ensuring a structured mechanism for addressing Centre-State issues.
 
 
 
• **Inter-State Council:**
 
 
• The Inter-State Council was established under **Article 263** of the Indian Constitution to facilitate coordination between the Union and States and resolve disputes.
 
• The council serves as a platform for discussing policies and strengthening federal governance in India.
 
• However, the council's role is advisory, and its recommendations are not binding on the Union or State governments.
 
 
 
• **Other Recommendations by Sarkaria Commission:**
 
 
• The Commission suggested that the role of the Governor should be limited to the constitutional framework, and they should not act as agents of the Centre.
 
• It emphasized cooperative federalism and recommended minimizing the misuse of Article 356, which allows for the imposition of President’s Rule in States.
 
• The financial relations between the Centre and the States were also reviewed, with recommendations to ensure fair distribution of resources.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other Committees and Commissions:**

 
 
• The **Rajamannar Committee**, established in **1969**, studied Centre-State relations and recommended reducing the Centre's dominance over the States.
 
• The **Punchhi Commission** (2007) also reviewed Centre-State relations and suggested several reforms, including revisiting the role of Governors and improving fiscal federalism.
 
• The **Venkatachelliah Commission**, set up in **2000**, focused on constitutional reforms to ensure better governance.
 
 
 
• **Relevance of Permanent Secretariat:**
 
 
• The establishment of a Permanent Secretariat for the Inter-State Council would provide necessary logistical and institutional support to the council, ensuring its smooth functioning.
 
• Such a secretariat would enable continuous monitoring and follow-up on the recommendations made during council meetings.

questions.question: How many types of Bihu festival are celebrated in Assam?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Bihu is a set of three important Assamese festivals in Assam – 'Rongali' or 'Bohag Bihu' observed in April, 'Kongali' or 'Kati Bihu' observed in October, and 'Bhogali' or 'Magh Bihu' observed in January.
 
• The Rongali Bihu is the most important of the three, celebrating the spring festival.
 
• The Bhogali Bihu or the Magh Bihu is a harvest festival, with community feasts.
 
• The Kongali Bihu or the Kati Bihu is the somber, thrifty one reflecting a season of short supplies and is an animistic festival.
 
• The Rongali Bihu coincides with the Assamese New year.
 
• Assamese celebrate the Rongali Bihu with feasts, music, and dancing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Bohag Bihu Or Rongali Bihu is one of the major festivals of Assam.
 
• Commonly known as Rongali Bihu, it is celebrated in Assam during the middle
 of the month of April.
 
• This festival celebrates the onset of the Assamese New Year (around April 15) and the coming of Spring.
 
• This marks the first day of the Hindu solar calendar and is also observed in Bengal, Manipur, Nepal, Orissa, Punjab, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu though called by different names like Pongal in south India, Baisakhi in north India.
 
• This festival is celebrated for the whole month.
 
• The new year of the Assamese calendar usually falls on April 15. The new year
 starts with the month of Bohag. This is the reason why Rongali Bihu is also called
 Bohag Bihu.
 
• The word Rongali is derived from Rong which means Happiness and celebrations. So this festival represents the happiness of society.
 
• On the eve of Rongali Bihu, the womenfolk clean their clothes and prepare special Bihu delicacies like Chira, Pitha, etc. In the rural areas, the menfolk remain busy collecting necessary items such as Tara Pogha (ropes for the cattle) prepared out of slices of Tara (an indigenous creeper) and vegetables such as raw turmeric, brinjal, gourd, etc for the next day's Garu Bihu.

questions.question: The last powerful Mughal emperor before the empire's decline was _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aurangzeb**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Aurangzeb (reigned 1658–1707)** was the last significant ruler of the Mughal Empire, under whom the empire reached its greatest territorial extent.
 
• He followed a strict interpretation of Islamic principles and imposed policies like the reintroduction of the Jizya tax on non-Muslims, which led to widespread dissatisfaction among his subjects.
 
• Despite being militarily successful, Aurangzeb’s prolonged wars, particularly in the Deccan region, drained the empire's resources and weakened its administrative structure.
 
• His centralized policies and intolerance toward certain cultural practices caused alienation among various communities, including the Marathas, Sikhs, and Rajputs, eventually leading to the decline of Mughal power.
 
• Aurangzeb's death in 1707 marked the beginning of the disintegration of the Mughal Empire, as his successors lacked the ability to govern the vast territories effectively.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Akbar (reigned 1556–1605):**

 
 
• Akbar is considered one of the greatest Mughal emperors, known for his policy of religious tolerance and efforts to foster unity among diverse communities in India.
 
• He introduced the Din-i-Ilahi, a syncretic religion aimed at blending elements of various faiths.
 
• Akbar’s administrative reforms, including the Mansabdari system, laid the foundation for a strong and centralized empire.
 
• His reign is often regarded as the Golden Age of the Mughal Empire due to cultural and economic prosperity.
 
 
 
• **Humayun (reigned 1530–1540 and 1555–1556):**
 
 
• Humayun was the second Mughal emperor who faced significant challenges, including military defeats against Sher Shah Suri.
 
• He was temporarily exiled but regained the throne in 1555 with the assistance of Persian allies.
 
• Humayun’s reign was marked by instability, and his untimely death led to Akbar ascending the throne at a young age.
 
 
 
• **Muhammad Shah (reigned 1719–1748):**
 
 
• Known as Muhammad Shah Rangila, he ruled during the later years of the Mughal Empire when its decline had already begun.
 
• His reign saw the invasion of Delhi by Nadir Shah of Persia in 1739, which significantly weakened the empire.
 
• Muhammad Shah's inability to address internal and external challenges further accelerated the fragmentation of Mughal authority.

questions.question: Which among the following is a wind instrument?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pava**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pava** is a traditional wind instrument that belongs to the family of musical instruments that produce sound by the vibration of air, typically using a player's breath.
 
• It is commonly used in various folk and classical performances and is known for its melodious and soothing sound.
 
• Unlike percussion instruments like **Dhol** or **Nagara**, which rely on striking a surface, wind instruments like the Pava generate sound through the manipulation of air.
 
• Wind instruments have a long history and are deeply embedded in cultural and musical traditions across the world. The Pava specifically is a part of traditional and cultural Indian music.
 
• Other examples of wind instruments include the flute, clarinet, and shehnai. These instruments often require a great deal of skill and breath control.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Dhol:**

 
 
• **Dhol** is a percussion instrument and not a wind instrument. It is widely used in folk music and celebrations, especially in North India, Punjab, and Pakistan.
 
• It consists of a cylindrical wooden shell covered with animal skin or synthetic material and is played using sticks.
 
• It is integral to Bhangra and other traditional dance forms.
 
 
 
• **Manjira:**
 
 
• **Manjira** is a traditional Indian percussion instrument made of a pair of small metallic cymbals.
 
• It is used to provide rhythmic accompaniment in devotional and folk music.
 
• Manjira is not a wind instrument as it produces sound through the striking of metal surfaces.
 
 
 
• **Nagara:**
 
 
• **Nagara** is a large drum that is also categorized as a percussion instrument.
 
• It is commonly used in religious ceremonies, folk performances, and traditional Indian music.
 
• Sound is generated by striking the drumhead with sticks, which makes it distinct from wind instruments.
 
 
 
• **Wind Instruments:**
 
 
• **Characteristics:** Wind instruments produce sound by the vibration of air inside a tube or body of the instrument.
 
• **Examples:** Flute, clarinet, saxophone, shehnai, and Pava.
 
• **Function:** The player blows air into or across an opening, and different notes are produced by changing the length of the air column inside the instrument.
 
• **Applications:** These instruments are widely used in classical, folk, and modern music across various cultures globally.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Significance:** Wind instruments have been used for centuries in rituals, religious ceremonies, and entertainment, showcasing their cultural importance.
 
• **Scientific Basis:** The sound in wind instruments is produced by the vibration of air columns, which is manipulated by changing the length of the column using finger holes or valves.
 
• **Global Examples:** Instruments like the flute (India), bagpipes (Scotland), and pan pipes (South America) highlight the diversity of wind instruments worldwide.

questions.question: In India, Financial Inclusion Index has ____ sub-indices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Financial Inclusion Index (FI-Index)** in India was introduced by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** in **July 2021** to measure the level of financial inclusion across the country.
 
• The FI-Index comprises **three sub-indices:** **Access, Usage,** and **Quality**. These sub-indices are weighted to provide a comprehensive score representing the state of financial inclusion.
 
• **Access:** This sub-index measures the extent of availability of financial services, including the number of bank branches, ATMs, and banking correspondents.
 
• **Usage:** It captures the frequency and volume of transactions by individuals and entities, reflecting the extent of utilization of financial services.
 
• **Quality:** It evaluates the quality aspects of financial inclusion, such as financial literacy, consumer protection, and the resolution of grievances related to financial services.
 
• The FI-Index is computed annually and ranges from **0 to 100**, where 0 denotes complete financial exclusion and 100 represents full financial inclusion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Objective of Financial Inclusion Index:**

 
 
• The FI-Index aims to provide policymakers and stakeholders with a comprehensive tool to assess the progress of financial inclusion and identify gaps for targeted interventions.
 
• It is a part of the broader initiative to achieve inclusive growth by bringing the unbanked population into the formal financial system.
 
 
 
• **Features of Financial Inclusion in India:**
 
 
• India has made significant strides in financial inclusion through initiatives such as the **Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY)**, which provides access to basic bank accounts.
 
• Other schemes like **Direct Benefit Transfers (DBT)** and **Digital India** have further enhanced financial inclusion by promoting digital payments and banking services.
 
 
 
• **Global Context of Financial Inclusion:**

questions.question: What is the name of the geographical area from which all precipitation flows into a single river system?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Drainage basin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **Drainage basin**, also known as a watershed or catchment area, is a geographical area where all precipitation, including rain, snow, and other forms of water, collects and flows into a single river system.
 
• The boundaries of a drainage basin are defined by **elevated landforms**, such as ridges or mountains, which direct the flow of water toward a particular river or its tributaries.
 
• Drainage basins are an essential aspect of hydrological studies as they help in understanding the flow of water, sediment transport, and nutrient cycles.
 
• Examples of major drainage basins in the world include the **Amazon Basin** (largest drainage basin in the world), the **Ganga-Brahmaputra Basin** in India, and the **Nile River Basin** in Africa.
 
• *Hence, "Drainage basin" is the correct answer.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Characteristics of a Drainage Basin:**

 
 
• The size of a drainage basin can vary from a few square kilometers to millions of square kilometers.
 
• Drainage basins often consist of a network of **tributaries**, smaller streams that feed into the main river.
 
• The water flow in a drainage basin is influenced by factors like **topography, climate, vegetation, and human activities**.
 
• Drainage basins serve as a critical source of water for agriculture, drinking, and industrial purposes.
 
 
 
• **Comparison of Other Options:**
 
 
• **Plateau:** A plateau is a flat, elevated landform that rises sharply above the surrounding area. It is not related to the collection of precipitation into a river system.
 
• **Waterfall zone:** This refers to an area where waterfalls are commonly found, usually due to steep gradients in rivers. It is not a geographical area where precipitation collects into a single river system.
 
• **Inland depression:** This is a low-lying area or a basin, often without an outlet to the sea. While it can collect water, it is not the same as a drainage basin, which specifically channels water to a river system.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Drainage Basins:**
 
 
• **Amazon Basin:** Located in South America, it is the largest drainage basin in the world, covering about 7 million square kilometers.
 
• **Mississippi River Basin:** Located in the United States, it is one of the largest drainage basins in North America.
 
• **Ganga-Brahmaputra Basin:** One of the most important drainage basins in India, supporting millions of people through its water resources.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of Drainage Basins:**

 
 
• Drainage basins play a critical role in **water resource management**, as they determine how water flows and is distributed across regions.
 
• They are essential for maintaining biodiversity, as they provide habitats for various aquatic and terrestrial species.
 
• Drainage basins are also used in the planning and construction of **dams and irrigation systems**, which are vital for agriculture and energy production.
 
 
 
• **Global Drainage Systems:**
 
 
• Approximately **64% of the world's freshwater** flows through drainage basins.
 
• Many drainage basins are transboundary, meaning they span across multiple countries, leading to international agreements for water-sharing.

questions.question: In a test, 40% of the students passed in Science; 50% passed in English; and 10% passed in both the subjects. Find the percentage of students who have failed.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total passed % = Passed in Science + Passed in English − Passed in both

Total passed % = 40% + 50% − 10% = 80%

Students who failed = Total students (100%) − Total passed %

Failed % = 100% − 80% = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Passed in Science, n(S) = 40%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/218596f8ea102154f397e965dd3445b35024cbaf79734fd2a9cf7d1a5951ccbf.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Passed in at least one subject = n(S ∪ E) = n(S) + n(E) − n(S ∩ E)

Failed % = 100% − n(S ∪ E)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Students passed in at least one subject = 40% + 50% − 10%

⇒ Students passed = 80%

⇒ Percentage of students who failed = 100% − 80% = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

Set Theory Basics

The formula for the union of two sets is n(A ∪ B) = n(A) + n(B) − n(A ∩ B).

De Morgan's Laws

The complement of the union of two sets is the intersection of their complements: (A ∪ B)' = A' ∩ B'. In this context, failing in both subjects is the complement of passing in at least one.
